title: "Get started"
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, ".")
```

This page takes a set of daily NetCDF files, opens them with xarray, writes a
VRT describing them as one cube, and reads it back through GDAL.

## Some files

Four daily files of sea surface temperature, each `(time, lat, lon)` with one
time step, stored as packed `int16` (the usual layout for gridded daily
products). The helper writes them to a temporary folder.

```{python}
import xarray as xr
from _fixtures import daily_netcdf

paths = daily_netcdf(n=4)
[p.name for p in paths]
```

## Open them as usual

```{python}
ds = xr.open_mfdataset(paths, combine="nested", concat_dim="time")
ds
```

xarray has decoded the packing (the values are floats) and the times
(`datetime64`), and remembers how they were stored in `.encoding`.

## Write the VRT

`write_mdim_vrt` needs the Dataset, the source files in order, an output path,
and how the files combine: here each file contributes its slice of an existing
`time` dimension, which is `composition="concat"`.

```{python}
from xvrt import write_mdim_vrt

out = write_mdim_vrt(
    ds, paths, paths[0].parent / "sst.vrt",
    composition="concat", concat_dim="time",
)
print(out.read_text())
```

A few things to notice:

- The data array is declared `Int16` with `<Scale>`, `<Offset>` and
  `<NoDataValue>`: the VRT reads the stored bytes, and GDAL applies the
  decoding, so nothing is lost or double-applied. See
  [Packed data](guide/packed-data.qmd).
- Regularly spaced coordinates are written as `<RegularlySpacedValues>`
  (start and step), not as lists.
- Time is written back in its original CF units, origin time of day
  included.
- Each `<Source>` states its extent (`<SourceSlab>`) and where it lands
  (`<DestSlab>`), so GDAL opens only the files a read needs.
- No CRS was found on this Dataset, so there is no `<SRS>` (xvrt warns). Pass
  `crs=` or see [CRS](guide/crs.qmd).

## Read it back

```{python}
from osgeo import gdal

gdal.UseExceptions()
vrt = gdal.OpenEx(str(out), gdal.OF_MULTIDIM_RASTER)
sst = vrt.GetRootGroup().OpenMDArray("sst")
print([d.GetName() for d in sst.GetDimensions()], [d.GetSize() for d in sst.GetDimensions()])
print("scale", sst.GetScale(), "nodata", sst.GetNoDataValueAsDouble(), "unit", sst.GetUnit())
```

The unscaled values match what xarray shows:

```{python}
import numpy as np

from_vrt = sst.GetUnscaled().ReadAsArray()
np.allclose(from_vrt, ds.sst.values)
```

The same file opens in any tool built on GDAL's multidimensional API, for
example `gdal mdim info sst.vrt` on the command line, or an xarray backend for
GDAL:

```{python}
xr.open_dataset(out, engine="gdalxarray")
```
